items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: another dear friend of ours named (Treservant) Simms, who played the bass sousaphone

ctx.x: In Dallas, Texas. And I used to play for the kids to march out for lunch time, and play for them to march back in, on -- you know, on my own, and I would be making up my rhythms, hurrup de bup de bup de bing, bom, brrrrrr, you know, just playing, and so maybe about when I got to the fourth grade there -- by this time, now, okay- My brother Kei, and a dear friend of ours named Herman Batts, that played the banjo, another dear friend of ours named (Treservant) Simms, who played the bass sousaphone, and another…

And gee, you know, the trumpet player, we called him Sap, because he was sort of a dumb cat, could really play. His last name was Wilson. He had a brother named Norris Wilson that played trombone, and you know, I've forgotten Sap's first name, but it may come to me --
